title: When the Orchard Breaks Revisited
premise: Marine biologist Beatrix Amberdale has spent a decade training her heart like any other muscle—contained, measurable, safe—after the orchard fire that destroyed her family's vineyard and her engagement to rival heir Julian Voss. When a snowstorm strands them both at the ruined estate, now half-restored by Julian's quiet redemption project, they are forced to confront the truth of that night: Julian's father set the fire, and Beatrix's testimony was buried by money. Digging through ledgers, scorched deeds, and their own tangled memories, they must decide whether justice outside the law is worth exposing both families. In the end, they choose truth over inheritance, testify together as the first harvest comes in, and risk the whole heart instead of lending pieces.
about_author: S. M. Vane is the pen name of a former agricultural archivist who spent years cataloguing land disputes in rural county records before turning to fiction. They write romance about people who mistake control for safety, and live near a working orchard they refuse to name.

chapters.title: Counting Turtles
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. On a research vessel, she catalogs sea turtle nesting data with clinical precision, narrating her philosophy of the trainable heart. A letter arrives: the Amberdale orchard has been sold—or nearly—to an anonymous buyer. Her hands shake for the first time in years. Emotional beat: controlled grief cracking open.

chapters.title: The Buyer's Signature
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian Voss reveals he is the buyer, restoring the burned vineyard as penance for his father's crimes. His board threatens to remove him if he doesn't flip the property for profit. He drives toward the orchard through worsening weather. Emotional beat: guilt disguised as strategy.

chapters.title: Whiteout
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. The storm closes the mountain road; Beatrix, arriving to contest the sale, and Julian are trapped together in the estate's crumbling farmhouse with no signal and one working fireplace. Old wounds surface fast—accusations, then an uneasy truce over canned peaches. Emotional beat: forced proximity igniting old chemistry.

chapters.title: What the Fire Kept
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Exploring the cellar, they find her mother's hidden strongbox: insurance documents suggesting arson was known and suppressed. Beatrix realizes Julian's father paid off the investigator—with money that built Julian's career. Emotional beat: betrayal recontextualized; the past becomes evidence.

chapters.title: Ledgers and Lies
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confirms it against his father's private ledgers and must choose: protect his family name or help Beatrix. He chooses her, burning his bridge with a midnight call to his lawyer. They share a kiss that feels like surrender. Emotional beat: first whole-hearted act.

chapters.title: The Interim Board
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. The storm lifts; Julian's board sends enforcers to secure the property and seize 'company documents'—the ledgers. Beatrix hides them in the turtle-lab cold storage back on the coast. She realizes loving Julian means becoming a target again. Emotional beat: fear versus resolve.

chapters.title: Lending Pieces
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian offers a deal: he'll take the fall alone, shielding Beatrix from litigation, repeating the old pattern of protection-as-control. She refuses—he cannot contain this heart for her. They fight bitterly beneath the bare vines. Emotional beat: love confronting its own bad habits.

chapters.title: Bud Break
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Spring: the surviving vines bud. Beatrix gathers witnesses—the retired investigator, a former fieldhand—and builds a case outside the courts: public records, press, the community that lost everything. Julian publicly confesses his family's role at the town meeting. Emotional beat: justice taking root.

chapters.title: The Hearing of the Orchard
chapters.summary: Alternating POV. Climax. The board sues; the state reopens the arson case. On the stand, Beatrix and Julian testify together, each corroborating the other across twenty years of silence. Julian's father breaks; the sale is voided, restitution ordered, the board collapses. Emotional beat: truth as the only winning move.

chapters.title: First Harvest
chapters.summary: Beatrix's POV. Autumn. The community harvests the restored orchard; Beatrix splits her life between the lab and the vines, refusing to choose between her two callings. She and Julian plant a new row named for what survived. The heart, she admits, was never containable—only waiting. Emotional beat: wholehearted resolution.
